candidates.title: Typhoon OCR 2: From Thai Document Transcription to Multilingual, Multi-Task OCR
candidates.content: Typhoon OCR 1.5 focused on reading Thai documents. However, in real-world workflows, users often need to extract specific information or preserve the structure of an entire page for further processing. Typhoon OCR 2 handles both tasks in a single model, with prompt-driven extraction and structured full-page parsing. Full-page parsing covers Thai, English, and Chinese. We release compact 2B and 0.8B models adapted from open document parsers through supervised fine-tuning on curated Thai and public multilingual data, followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with task rewards and a rule penalizing unfinished responses. Among evaluated open models, Typhoon OCR 2 2B scores highest on Thai MDPBench (80.7 versus 68.9 for Typhoon OCR 1.5) and on ThaiOCRBench (59.91 versus 40.45), which covers recognition, extraction, and document understanding. The 2B model remains close to its base on English olmOCR-bench (84.7 versus 84.4) and on OmniDocBench, which evaluates English and Chinese together (90.97 versus 91.03). candidates.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
candidates.content: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the agent is exposed to beyond what the task reads or writes; and feature coverage, the application features beyond what the task uses. Existing works set each dimension on engineering grounds, but they do not measure its effect on training. How complete must an environment be to train a capable agent, and along which dimensions? In MobileGym, we adjust each dimension separately, train Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, and evaluate every policy in the original full environment. A verifier that rewards only one reference path lowers success by 10.53 points, and removing unneeded records also lowers success. candidates.title: Rapid degradation of six class I HDAC complexes reveals a mixture of unique, cooperative, and antagonistic roles
candidates.content: Abstract The class I histone deacetylases (HDACs) 1, 2, and 3 form seven families of distinct large multiprotein complexes that regulate gene expression via deacetylation of lysines in histone tails. The degree of redundancy and functional overlap between complexes and their acute gene targets remain unknown. We used CRISPR/Cas9 to create six cell lines in which individual HDAC complexes were tagged with FKBP12 F36V enabling rapid (<1 h), PROTAC-mediated, degradation. RNA sequencing at 6 h reveals that together, the four major complexes (CoREST, NuRD, NCoR/SMRT, and SIN3A) perturbed >50% of expressed genes. More than 60% of these are regulated by a single complex. ChIP-sequencing revealed that >54% of differentially expressed genes are directly regulated by the associated complex. Of genes regulated by more than one complex, approaching 50% are reciprocally regulated such that HDAC complexes act as antagonistic regulators. Homer analysis strongly suggests that the complexes are reliant on different transcription factors. candidates.title: Reprogramming mRNA localization by targeted RNA-protein interference reveals roles in oncogenesis
candidates.content: Abstract RNA binding proteins (RBPs) associate with RNAs in intricate ribonucleoprotein complexes and regulate various aspects of RNA life cycle and, by extension, cell functions. Despite their significance, elucidating the functional contributions of specific RNA–RBP binding events, particularly in long-term phenotypic assays, remains challenging. Here, we harness the specificity of CRISPR/dCas13 to interfere with specific RNA–RBP interactions. We apply this methodology to GA-rich mRNA localization elements which recruit the RNA-binding protein CNBP and serve as platforms for the assembly of mRNA trafficking complexes. We show that dCas13/gRNA binds to target transcripts in a highly specific manner and interferes with CNBP recruitment leading to altered target mRNA localization and cell motility, consistent with the function of the targeted mRNAs. We describe optimizations and considerations for the stable implementation of this system. We further use it to show that interfering with the localization of the GA-containing NET1 mRNA reduces cancer cell invasiveness and metastatic lung colonization. candidates.title: Translons upstream of protein-coding regions rather than their products are crucial for proliferation of human cells of distinct origin
candidates.content: Abstract Upstream open reading frames (uORFs) are a widespread class of translated regions (translons) occurring in 5′ leaders of messenger RNAs. They serve critical roles in post-transcriptional regulation and some are known to encode small proteins and peptideins. Yet it is not known which of these modes of function is more critical for human cells. We conducted a CRISPR-Cas9 mutagenesis screening targeting 969 translated human uORFs across three cell lines of distinct origin. Disruption of 155 uORFs impaired cell proliferation, although these effects were highly cell-type specific, with only six shared across all cell lines. Neither evolutionary conservation, comparative protein-coding potential, nor population mutational constraint distinguished uORF hits. Instead, high-throughput analysis of CRISPR-induced mutations combined with reporter assays demonstrated that proliferation phenotypes arise from altered cis -regulation of coding sequence (CDS) translation.
